description: Fetch one public web page and return its readable text as clean markdown or plain text, with navigation, scripts, headers and footers stripped. When to use: you have a specific URL (from web_search or the user) and need what the page actually says - 'read this article', 'summarise this docs page', 'turn this URL into markdown'. Do not use: to crawl or mirror a site, to fetch a page behind a login or paywall, to read API/RPC endpoints, or for book text inside CyberLibrary (use cyberlibrary_get_chapter). Returns: {url, final_url, status, title, content, chars, truncated, fetched_at, source (direct|provider), cached, took_ms, _metering}. The response is capped at 12000 characters per call; raise max_chars (up to 20000) when you need more. Reads one public URL only, respects robots.txt, and does not bypass login or paywall. Direct fetch is tried first; pages blocked from this node are fetched through a provider and marked source=provider. Metered: all web tools share 100 free calls/day per IP (separate from the risk/library allowance), then 1 credit per call over x402 - there is no API key; the 402 answer carries accepts[].

max_chars.description: Truncate the returned content to this many characters (2000-20000). Default 8000.

ocr.description: Force OCR on scanned PDFs/images (auto-detected by default; set false to skip).

url.description: The http(s) URL to read (max 2048 chars).

name: web_fetch
